stage_a.note: The founders are smiling, enthusiastic, and confident throughout the prepared presentation.
They show strong engagement with the problem their product solves.
The founders are very friendly and approachable, smiling as they present.

venture.description: Heel caps that prevent high heels from sinking into grass or getting stuck in cracks.
venture.note: The founders ask for $500,000 for a 10% equity stake to expand their heel protector business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves, state their ask, and explain the problem their heel protectors solve for women.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks Becca if she is currently wearing the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca confirms that both founders are wearing the heel protectors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica offers samples of the product to the investors.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori notes that the founders are wearing dark protectors on dark heels and asks about clear ones.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica confirms they offer clear protectors as well as black, silver, and gold.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks how much the heel protectors cost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica states that each pair retails for $10 and the box containing three pairs costs $30.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert questions the $30 price tag for the box.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica confirms the price.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori remarks that their margins must be incredible.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca invites the investors, including the men, to come up and try out the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks if they have shoes in his size.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica confirms they have shoes for the male investors, and a demonstration ensues on the artificial grass.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks the founders about their background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica explains that she and Becca met working at Goldman Sachs right out of college.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks what happened after they worked at Goldman Sachs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica and Becca note they learned a lot there, especially that they should know who to go to for help.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin challenges their $5 million valuation and asks them to justify it with metrics.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca answers that they did $1.1 million in revenue last year and are on track for up to $1.5 million.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks where they are selling their product to achieve that revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica explains they are in 3,000 retail doors, including major retailers, and are correlated with the wedding industry.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin questions if they are making any cash flow yet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica states they have broken even and have 65% gross profit margins.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how much the founders have personally invested.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca explains they invested $100,000 together when they quit their jobs.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how much they have raised.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca states they have raised just under a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks how they raised the money.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca replies that they raised it from friends.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how many partners are involved in the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca states that she and Monica own 80% together.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert compliments the product and thanks them.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert points out that sales will increase with convenience and asks if they sell to hotels or wedding planners.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica confirms they sell to venues and hotels.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks how they will expand their distribution and suggests they need to hire a team.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca admits it is a bandwidth issue, as there are only the two of them and one full-time employee.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks what role the full-time person fulfills.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca clarifies that she is their operations manager.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark points out a discrepancy in their high gross margins and small team, asking where the money is going.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica explains they pay third-party contractors like graphic designers and web developers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks what their net profit was.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca replies that their net profit was $30,000.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert expresses surprise at the low net profit figure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks how much the founders paid themselves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica states they paid themselves $80,000 each last year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin acknowledges the salaries explain the low net profit.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori argues that the product is not a strong need because only a fraction of women wear spiky heels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica counters that when women do wear stilettos, the product acts as a necessary insurance policy to protect expensive shoes.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori states she does not think the problem is big enough to make it the right investment and exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark explains he does not believe they can reach the sales needed to justify the valuation and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica insists they believe in the business and are fully committed to it.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca adds that they are confident they can scale to 50 million in sales.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond argues that expanding to that level would eat profits and take too long, so he exits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert praises the idea as a new category and offers $500,000 for 25% equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori notes that there is only one investor left.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin offers $100,000 for 10% equity along with a $400,000 loan, valuing the company at $1 million.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert criticizes Kevin's offer, warning the founders against taking on debt.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica counters Robert's offer, asking if he would accept 20% equity instead.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks if 5% really makes a difference to them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica explains that it allows them to maintain a slight majority cumulatively.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert acknowledges their reasoning regarding ownership.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert agrees to their counter offer to close the deal before Kevin can interject.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders enthusiastically accept Robert's revised offer.

decisions.note: Does not believe the problem is big enough and it is not the right investment for her.
The numbers don't add up and he doesn't see them reaching $50 million in sales.
Believes the net profit will drop with expansion and they would have to sustain $5M for 10 years.
Believes they are creating a new category and wants to help them scale.
Believes the business is only worth $1 million.
Wants to maintain a slight majority cumulatively.
Agrees to the counter offer to close the deal.

record.notes: Kevin makes an offer but the founders counter and accept Robert's offer before Kevin can formalize an exit or further negotiation.
